Read out of saint.gr's line for 31 Ιουλίου, «Όσιος Ευδόκιμος ο Δίκαιος», with the rank word and the byname left off. The page glosses the name from ευ + δοκώ: the well-approved and praiseworthy, the glorious one.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 31 iulie — «Sfântul și Dreptul Evdochim»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 31ης Ιουλίου — «Όσιος Ευδόκιμος ο Δίκαιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 31 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: born in Cappadocia, of the parents Βασίλειος and Ευδοκία, rich and pious, dead at thirty-three — the Basil and Eudocia and the age the Romanian life gives. saint.gr adds four things that account does not. It dates him, «έδρασε κατά τους χρόνους του αυτοκράτορα Θεόφιλου (829 - 842 μ.Χ.)», and a `dates` object is proposed from that reign and from nothing else. It makes his office stratopedarch of Cappadocia first and then of the whole empire, where the Romanian life has him commander of the army of Cappadocia in the province of Charsianon. It dates the translation of the relic to Constantinople, «την 6η Ιουλίου 831 μ.Χ.» — which is a translation and not a feast of his, and is recorded here rather than drafted. And it says a portion of the saint is at the Great Lavra of the Holy Mountain, while of the body as a whole «Δεν είναι γνωστό πότε και κάτω από ποιες συνθήκες το Λείψανο διαλύθηκε». No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both of which name him, and both are taken; its megalynarion and its kathisma are kinds the schema does not hold and are not drafted.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Cel Ce te-a chemat pe tine de pe pământ la cereştile locaşuri păzeşte şi după moarte nevătămat trupul tău, sfinte; că tu, cu curăţie şi cu cinstită viaţă, fericite, ai vieţuit, nespurcându-ţi trupul, pentru aceasta, cu îndrăznire roagă pe Hristos Dumnezeu să ne mântuiască pe noi.

english.text: He who called you from earth to the dwellings of heaven keeps your body unharmed even after death, O saint; for you lived, blessed one, in purity and in an honourable life, and did not defile your body. Therefore with boldness pray to Christ God that we may be saved.

hymns.text: Ἐκ γῆς ὁ καλέσας σε, πρὸς αἰωνίους μονάς, τηρεῖ καὶ μετὰ θάνατον ἀδιαλώβητον, τὸ σῶμά σου, Ἅγιε, σὺ γὰρ ἐν σωφροσύνῃ, καὶ σεμνῇ πολιτείᾳ, μάκαρ ἐπολιτεύσω, μὴ μολύνας τὴν σάρκα· διὸ ἐν παῤῥησίᾳ Χριστῷ, πρέσβευε σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first hymn on the page of «Όσιος Ευδόκιμος ο Δίκαιος». It names no other saint and is addressed to him

english.text: He who called you from earth to the eternal mansions keeps your body undefiled even after death, O holy one; for you lived, blessed man, in chastity and in a sober way of life, and did not defile the flesh. Therefore with boldness intercede with Christ that we be saved.

hymns.text: Ἡ σεπτή σου σήμερον, ἡμᾶς συνήθροισε μνήμη, ἐν τῇ θείᾳ λάρνακι, τῶν ἱερῶν σου λειψάνων· πάντες οὖν, οἱ προσιόντες καὶ προσκυνοῦντες, ἅπασαν, δαιμόνων βλάβην ἀποσοβοῦνται, καὶ ποικίλων νοσημάτων, λυτροῦνται τάχος μάκαρ Εὐδόκιμε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — the second hymn on the page of «Όσιος Ευδόκιμος ο Δίκαιος», and it names him

english.text: Your venerable memory has gathered us today at the holy casket of your sacred relics; and so all who draw near and venerate are kept from every harm of demons, and are quickly delivered from many kinds of sickness, blessed Eudocimus.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Ευδόκιμος γεννήθηκε στη Καππαδοκία και έδρασε κατά τους χρόνους του αυτοκράτορα Θεόφιλου (829 - 842 μ.Χ.)». The bounds are the reign the page prints and not years of his own; it gives no year of birth and none of death, only that he died in his thirty-third year, and it dates the translation of his relic to 6 July 831.
